newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares rise, horizontal trend expected.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares rise, horizontal trend expected.

text.p: Polish shares extended Friday's gains on Monday and analysts said they were likely to stabilise until a new, strong signal emerges and pushes the market in either direction.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 107.4 points, or 0.8 percent, to 14,039.4, but turnover inched down 5.9 percent to 99.3 million zlotys ($36.2 million) on both markets as 49 issues rose, 13 fell and 15 were flat.

"The strong growth trend we had last month was stopped and now we are facing a stabilisation phase until positive or negative information appears on the market," said Mateusz Andrzejewski, an analyst at Pekao SA brokerage.
Analysts said the market was likely to swing in a channel between 13,600 and 14,300 of the WIG index until a new trend emerges.
Pekao's Andrzejewski said that the companies' August earning reports due in two weeks might be a strong signal for the market if they turn out to be especially good or bad.

Some analysts also said that after the end of the summer holiday season new investors were likely to bring more cash to the market and push it to a new high up from July 5's WIG record 14,282.2 points.
Three stocks traded live on Monday but stayed flat in a 79,800-zloty turnover ($29,120).

Mass privatisation NFI units fell 1.6 percent both in the single price aution system in 13.9-million-zloty ($5.1 million) trade and in continuous trade, which amounted to 1.4-million zlotys ($0.5 million).
